newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 70-80 bcf in wkly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 70-80 bcf in wkly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 70-80 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said this week.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged from 40 bcf to 105 bcf for the week ended February 28.
Traders said pressure to trim stocks in the East may be partly offset in this report by producer region injections due to favorable spreads, complicating this week's estimates.
"A lot depends on the producer region, and I think you'll see a net injection there," said a Texas-based trader.

In last report, overall stocks fell by 63 bcf, slightly below expectations, and were still 144 bcf, or 16 percent, above year-ago. Eastern storage last week stood 225 bcf, or 56 percent, over last year. The four week average draw is 108 bcf.

For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by just 62 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would cut the overall surplus to 1996 to about 130 bcf. Eastern storage fell by 27 bcf last year, while producing stocks dropped by 12 bcf and western stocks by 23 bcf.
